question: On 28 and 29 September 2026, Egyptian authorities arrested the entire newsroom of Matsadaash on the basis of ambiguous charges1. During their hearing before the Supreme State Security Prosecution2, the journalists declared that they had faced torture during their interrogation at National Security Agency facilities, including beatings, forced stripping, electric shocks and threats to harm them or their families. 1.
What action has the Commission taken towards the Egyptian authorities following the arrest of the Matsadaash journalists?

In July 2026, the Commission disbursed EUR 1.5 billion of macro-financial assistance to Egypt. In its information note to the European Parliament and the Council, the Commission stated that progress had been made with regard to the precondition of respecting democracy, the rule of law and human rights. In the light of these recent developments, would the Commission reassess this conclusion or does it continue to consider that Egypt is making progress in this area?

Can the Commission guarantee that any further disbursement of macro-financial assistance will remain suspended at least until the Matsadaash journalists, as well as other journalists detained for carrying out their professional activities, have been released?
